react_result.final_narrative_text: Seven metabolites significantly altered in the treatment group converge on pyrimidine metabolism as the dominant biological response. The strongest cross-paradigm signal is Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621), which achieved RaMP ORA rank 0 with an FDR of 1.12e-10, driven by four reduced pyrimidine derivatives: 5,6-dihydrouracil (C00429), 2'-deoxyuridine (C00526), 2'-deoxycytidine (C00881), and 3-ureidoisobutyric acid (C05100). This same metabolic theme repeats in the KEGG human pyrimidine pathway (hsa00240), which was the top hit in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 0.0003) and also appeared in RaMP ORA (rank 4, FDR 1.12e-10). Mummichog's empirical-compound network independently ranked Pyrimidine metabolism first (p = 0.00118, 10 of 11 pathway members hit), capturing the same five pyrimidine-derived drivers plus 5,6-dihydrothymine (C00906). The convergent finding across ORA, m/z-direct, and KEGG PSEA paradigms — all returning pyrimidine metabolism as the top hit — indicates that the treatment group experiences a systemic perturbation of pyrimidine catabolism, consistent with either increased degradation of pyrimidine bases and nucleosides or a block in their downstream processing. Guanidoacetic acid and oxalic acid each hit only in peripheral single-paradigm pathways (glycine/serine/alanine metabolism, glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism) and do not replicate across methods, suggesting they are secondary or treatment-specific rather than core pathway drivers.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Seven metabolites were significantly altered between control and treatment groups: dihydrothymine (KEGG C00906), deoxyuridine (KEGG C00526), deoxycytidine (KEGG C00881), ureidoisobutyric acid (KEGG C05100), dihydrouracil (KEGG C00429), guanidoacetic acid (KEGG C00581), and oxalic acid (KEGG C00209). Run_ramp_enrichment identified Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621) as the top pathway with an FDR score of 1.12e-10. Four metabolites appeared in the metabolites_hit list: 2'-deoxyuridine (CHEBI:16450, HMDB0000012), 2'-deoxycytidine (CHEBI:15698, HMDB0000014), 3-ureidoisobutyric acid (CHEBI:1670, HMDB0002031), and 5,6-dihydrouracil (CHEBI:15901, HMDB0000076). The same four metabolites also appeared in Pyrimidine metabolism (KEGG:map00240) at rank 4, which shares the identical FDR score of 1.12e-10, indicating the two pathway names describe overlapping compound coverage. Guanidoacetic acid and oxalic acid appeared only in peripheral pathways with broader scope, including Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1430728) and Biochemical pathways: part I (WP:WP3604), but were absent from the top-ranking pyrimidine-specific hits. The convergent finding across the top-ranking ORA hits indicates a systemic perturbation of pyrimidine catabolism.
